firing.source:
declare let a: any, b: any;
export const v = [] ?? a;

findings.message: The left side of this short-circuit always has the same truthiness or nullishness, so the operator never chooses: one side always wins and the other is dead. The usual cause is a guard written against the wrong thing, such as testing an object that is always present rather than the field inside it.

clean.source:
declare let a: any, b: any;
export const v = 1 < 2;
